description:
Controlled multi-token concept benchmark for the generative J-cone steering validation. Each example names a concept whose surface form spans multiple tokenizer pieces.

HARD REQUIREMENT: every target must tokenize to 2-6 tokens under the pinned Gemma tokenizer. This is enforced at run time by jlens.generative.validate_target_tokens (after the model loads, since the count is a property of the checkpoint vocabulary) and can be checked cheaply beforehand with scripts/validate_benchmark_targets.py. A single-token target tests no multi-token scoring, and because every steering schedule injects identically at the prompt-final position and differs only at generated positions, it forces prompt_only / constant / decaying to identical target log-probabilities. The original 'dev-split-photosynthesis' did exactly this (it tokenized to the single id 93036), so single common words were replaced with rarer, morphologically complex forms that segment reliably.

ORDERING IS SIGNIFICANT: --smoke runs the first example of a split and borrows the second as its unrelated-cone donor, so each split leads with multi-word targets, which cannot collapse to one token. Unrelated-cone donors are always drawn from the same split (see jlens.generative.select_split_examples) - a development run must never borrow a held-out example's cone.

'dev' is the calibration split (layer/strength search); 'heldout' is scored only after calibration is frozen. target_token_ids are resolved at run time against the pinned Gemma tokenizer (with the leading space as written in target_phrase) and recorded in every result together with the per-token strings; they are null here so the manifest stays tokenizer-revision-agnostic. control_prompt is a syntactically matched prompt evoking a different concept, used by the activation_diff condition. manual_subcone, when non-null, maps a source layer (as a string key) to indices into the example's active generator list (selection order); it names a candidate semantic group, not a proven binding.
